checksums.name: footer_block_0x3ff_tail
checksums.formula_detail: Trialed sum8/sum16/sum32/xor8/crc32/two's-complement-sum32 over block 0 (offset 0x0-0x3F) against stored bytes 0x1FFC-0x1FFF (both LE and BE u32 interpretations); no trial matched. Only one non-blank .sav sample exists, so no formula can be statistically confirmed.

io_driver_functions.notes: Generic DMA3 transfer primitive shared by both read and write paths: saves/restores IME, programs SAD/DAD/CNT registers (src=param1, dst=param2, count|0x80000000=param3), polls CNT_H enable bit (0x8000) until the transfer completes.

EEPROM 8-byte block read: clocks an address-request bitstream out via FUN_0805cf48, clocks 68 response bits back in, unpacks into 4x16-bit words (MSB-first) written to the caller's output buffer in reverse word order.

EEPROM 8-byte block write: serializes request+payload(4x u16)+address bitstream, clocks it out via FUN_0805cf48, then busy-waits on EEPROM write-ready bit using VCOUNT (0xE4 scanline wraparound) with a bounded timeout; param_3 selects retry-forever vs. single-timeout behavior.

Thin wrapper forcing FUN_0805d08c's blocking-retry flag to 1. Not present as an edge in ghidra/callgraph.json (missing edge found only by grep of decompiled.c). No caller of this wrapper was found anywhere in the traced 43-function set - the save trigger is outside visibility.

Read-and-verify: calls FUN_0805cfc8 to read a block, compares all 4 words against an expected buffer, returns 0x8000 on mismatch else 0. No caller found in the traced set (confirmed empty in callgraph.json and by grep).

fuzzing_targets.mutation: flip one byte of the candidate magic (e.g. 0x13 -> 0x00)
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If this is a validity magic, game should treat the save as absent/corrupt and boot as if from the blank cap-00 state; no change would falsify the magic hypothesis

fuzzing_targets.mutation: write non-zero bytes into the currently all-zero reserved region, leaving the magic untouched
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If this region is a real payload field, UI/title-screen/save-select state should visibly differ; if it is padding, no observable change is expected

fuzzing_targets.mutation: flip one byte of the footer (e.g. 0x2e -> 0x2f)
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If consumed as a checksum/integrity field on load, game should reject/reset the save like a magic failure; if it's an unchecked counter/ID, no observable difference

fuzzing_targets.mutation: write a distinguishable non-erased value (e.g. 0xAAAAAAAA) then force another in-game save event
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If the game always writes the full 8-byte block 0x3FF together, a subsequent save should restore 0xFFFFFFFF there, proving it's an actively managed field rather than untouched erased space

open_questions: No caller of FUN_0805d078 (blocking EEPROM write wrapper) or FUN_0805d1ec (read+verify) was found anywhere in the traced 43-function decompilation - the game-specific save trigger, target block-address selection, and in-RAM save-struct population logic are completely outside this trace's visibility.
ghidra/callgraph.json is missing at least one real call edge (0x0805d078 -> 0x0805d08c), found only by manual grep of decompiled.c; treat the provided callgraph as a lower bound, not exhaustive.

The 0x1337C0DE magic candidate at offset 0x0004 has no located writer or comparator in code; it is inferred purely from being the only distinctive non-zero value in an otherwise all-zero 64-byte record.

The footer bytes at offset 0x1FFC-0x1FFF do not match any trialed sum/xor/crc32 formula over the candidate header region; with only one non-blank .sav sample, no checksum hypothesis can be statistically confirmed either way.
Whether the first half of EEPROM block 0x3FF (offset 0x1FF8-0x1FFB, currently 0xFFFFFFFF) was deliberately written or never touched cannot be determined from the available samples.
EEPROM blocks 0x008-0x3FE are blank in all available captures; whether/how they are ever used by the game is unknown.

The runtime EEPROM address bit-width (6-bit vs 14-bit protocol variant), read from *(byte*)(ptr+8) in both FUN_0805cfc8 and FUN_0805d08c, could not be resolved to a concrete constant because the backing _DAT_* pointers' initialization is not present in the traced function set.
